result.message: Code review of the round-2 best kernel (subject cc149ba4…, value_selecting_reduction_backward) against the supplied catalog definition, oracle, workload lists (78 correctness / 18 timing) and the two-round optimize ledger. The candidate implements the aten semantics out[o,r,i] = grad[o,i] if indices[o,i]==r else 0 (equivalent to zeros+scatter, which is injective here) with one Triton kernel, allocates a fresh output (no input mutation, no alias, no torch.ops fallback), performs no host synchronization or environment mutation, and uses no test-derived shapes; the measured evidence (96/96 PASSED, max_abs_error 0.0, geo_mean 1.602 with min_speedup 1.383) is consistent with an exact-match selection kernel and with reference/candidate measured separately. No P0 test-contract or conversion defect was found. Three advisory P1 findings are recorded: (a) inputs whose grad/indices layout is not affinely collapsible raise NotImplementedError, narrowing the operator's domain relative to aten (a permuted/sliced layout is not covered by the single strided workload pattern); (b) output offsets are computed in Triton's 32-bit integer arithmetic, so outputs above 2^31 elements would silently overflow (exercised maximum is 8192^2 ≈ 67M); (c) the supplied workload set never exercises the nb>1 tiling branch (requires sizes[dim] > 8192), nor nd==1 / zero-size / sizes[dim]==1 shapes. The optimize-side review_tests attempt is explicitly SKIPPED_EXPLICIT (subject 83d123…), so its evaluate.json reference-parity run (geo_mean 1.008) does not add independent validation of this candidate; candidate validation rests on .ledger.json round 2.
